title: candidate fit uncertainty pulse - nina patel
content:
Quick brain dump after the loop with candidate (initials: C.T.). Mostly for my own calibration; will extract the crisp feedback later. 

Context / role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving, KV cache, batching, SLOs). Loop included architecture dive, a systems design whiteboard, and a short take-home overview we gave them. Interviewers: Aria (serving performance), Samir (SRE patterns), me (runtime & product tradeoffs).

High-level gut: mixed — clear systems intuition but some shaky assumptions about cache coherence under preemption and model sharding. Good in debugging/live triage; weaker on proactive design for graceful degradation and capacity planning.

What they did well:
- Comfortable with latency budgets: talked in p99/kg terms and sketched how to instrument (prometheus + p99 histograms).
- Practical on batching heuristics: proposed adaptive batching with a small backoff for tail-latency control (simple, implementable).
- Debug flow: when we gave a token-storm scenario, they walked through KV eviction and cache warmup reasoning step-by-step, found a few low-hanging bugs in our hypothetical impl.

Concerns / uncertainty signals:
- KV cache correctness under preempt+recreate: assumed a single authoritative cache source; didn't account for transient duplicated in-flight requests during node replacement. Sketch omitted versioning/lease model and impact on at-least-once semantics.
- Quantization & kernel selection: high-level suggestions but no concrete experience with quantization-aware runtime work (e.g., int8 perf tradeoffs, calibration). Could ramp but partial gap here.
- Metrics granularity: defaulted to token-level counters; didn't discuss token sampling/trace correlation needed to debug customer regressions at scale.

Behavioral / culture fit notes:
- Calm under pressure, thoughtful clarifying questions.
- Prefers pragmatic, incremental wins over big-bang redesigns — aligns with product velocity but may under-invest in corner-case correctness unless prompted.

Scorecard (quick, rough):
- Technical (systems): 3/5 — good pragmatic systems sense, misses some deeper distributed-cache invariants.
- Debugging: 4/5 — clear, methodical live troubleshooting.
- Exper. with inference-specific infra (quantization, kernels): 2/5 — needs mentorship or proof of ramp.
- Communication / collaboration: 4/5 — concise, engages interviewers.

Suggested interview follow-ups / next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive focused on cache correctness: ask them to design a lease/versioning mechanism for KV caches across preemptible workers, including failure modes and how the control plane coordinates invalidations. (owner: Aria)
2) Small take-home: a short design doc (1–2 pages) comparing two options for fallback behavior under capacity saturation (model-variants vs degraded-serving) with cost/latency tradeoffs. (owner: me)
3) If we proceed, pair them with an infra engineer for a short paid exercise on quantization pipeline basics (calibration, accuracy check). This will validate ramp.

Bias & calibration notes (for panel):
- Risk of anchoring: interviewers praised pragmatic suggestions; make sure we didn't overweight "ship-it" bias and ignore distributed correctness gaps.
- Recency bias: they performed strongly in the live debug (fresh in memory); ensure follow-up covers the weaker technical facets.

Open questions I still have:
- Have they shipped any production inference feature that involved kernel selection decisions? (resume line ambiguous.)
- Depth of exposure to long-tail customer regressions — can they author precise evals and regression alerts?

Draft feedback blurb for panel (short):
"Candidate shows strong pragmatic systems instincts and is excellent at live troubleshooting. There are gaps around distributed cache correctness and inference-specific performance knobs (quantization/kernel choices). I recommend a focused technical follow-up around KV cache correctness and a short learning exercise for quantization to determine ramp potential. Not an immediate yes without those checks."

Notes-to-self: capture the cache-version sketch from the follow-up (I want to see explicit lease/epoch model and how they handle split-brain on control-plane failover). Also link to JIRA-ENG-3472 since some of the same failure modes we discussed are tracked there.

Action items (me):
- Draft follow-up prompt by 2025-03-04.
- Ping Aria to own cache deep-dive scheduling (Aria owns, cc Samir).
- Save this note under candidate folder and move to panel when follow-up is decided.

Timestamped quick log: 2025-02-14 22:10 PST — finished panel, brain tired, notes raw. 2025-02-18 — chatted with Aria briefly, she also had cache concerns. 2025-02-25 — added take-home suggestion.

Misc links / references I want to paste into follow-up payload: 
- JIRA-ENG-3472 (token-storm + cache races)
- internal doc: "runtime-cache-lease-patterns" (confluence id: 89012)
- GH PR we referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-runtime/pull/582

End of dump.
